# `union-branch-added`

oneOf/anyOf branch added

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` in requests, `warn` in responses |
| **Rule IDs** | `union-branch-added` (both directions), `union-branch-added-in-request`, `union-branch-added-in-response` |
| **Status** | Planned (M5) |
| **Group** | Schemas ([RULES.md section 7](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A branch was added to a `oneOf` or `anyOf`. Branches are matched by discriminator value, `$ref` target or structure, not by position.

## Why this default

In requests: more values are valid. In responses: clients receive a variant they were not written to handle.

## Example

_No example yet: one is added with the rule's test case when the rule is implemented._

## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file, for the generic ID or any variant ID above (the more specific ID wins). The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  union-branch-added: warn
```

## How to fix

Only return the new variant to clients that support it.
